surviving.summary: AC1 requires the box to pass *every* setupGate gate, which includes gate A (git HEAD prefix-match + empty porcelain). That depends on a dispatched, filled box, not on the image — so AC1's e2e is implicitly a full DF3.1 dispatch, not a bare boot. Stronger rather than weaker, but the dependency is unstated and a dev agent may read 'boot the image and run setupGate' as sufficient.

AC7a's clone-arm is unpriced. R6 §7 says the pullable-vs-clone answer 'materially changes the story's size' (cloning drags in exeuntu's own unpinned Go/fd/catalog fetches, making our digest a pin over a non-reproducible build). The story records which shape shipped but states no re-point or split trigger, so a 5 SP estimate silently absorbs the worse arm.

The `--registry-auth` private arm's PAT has an owner and an expiry named but no rotation *cadence* and no runbook reference (secrets checklist: 'Rotate manually without a runbook is a HIGH finding'). Mitigated to MEDIUM because the arm is default-off, gated behind a recorded ratified deviation, and the Deviation bullet states an expired PAT breaks every box create at once — but the cadence itself is unowned.

Observability Contract uses `{ requestId, runId, ... }` while the shipped emit at driver.ts:274 uses `{ vm: name, ... }`. Same value (create's `name` is the run id, assertValidRunId-checked), so this is a field-naming inconsistency the implementer must reconcile, not a semantic gap. Left as-is because the three-bullet `runId` shape is the format authority's fixed template.

Test fixtures for the registry-auth validation path are not required to use obviously-fake sentinel values (secrets checklist: 'Fixture secrets are obviously fake'). Low risk here because the default path carries no credential at all and the DoD already forbids the value appearing in any emitted line or provenance field.

cross_boundary_notes: DF1.10 — `EnvironmentFile=%h/app/.env` appears in four places (df1-10 AC3 :71, Infra Prereq :113, Technical Notes :124, DoD :186). DF2.10 now ships a *system* unit with `User=exedev` and the literal `/home/exedev/app/.env`, because `%h` in a system unit is the manager's home (/root), not `User=`'s. DF1.10 must change those four references or it documents a unit that fails to start.

DF1.10 — its DoD/e2e says the run boots 'DF2.10's pinned image'. DF1.10 adds the engine build stage to `oci/exedev/Dockerfile`, which changes the digest; it boots a *re-pinned* rebuild, and it inherits DF2.10's pin ritual (publish workflow records the digest<->buildId pair). DF2.10's DoD was corrected to say so; DF1.10's wording still reads as booting the identical artifact.

DF1.11 — AC2(c) requires the re-provisioned `/etc/tmpfiles.d/qds-steering.conf` to be a *byte-identical* no-op against DF2.10's baked file, but AC2(a) writes `d /run/steering 0700 <uid> <gid>` (ids resolved on the box) while DF2.10 bakes the ADR's literal `d /run/steering 0700 exedev exedev` (names). Numeric ids and names are not byte-identical. DF2.10 kept the ADR's form and fixed it normatively; DF1.11 must converge on those bytes or drop the byte-identical claim.

DF1.11 — INV-IBOX-13 requires `QDS_STEERING_ROOT` unset in the engine's systemd unit, and DF3.7 AC4 requires `QDS_RUN_ROOT` unset in the box. Neither story can enforce a property of an artifact DF2.10 ships; DF2.10 now carries it as an explicit AC6 obligation. Both siblings can cite it rather than assume it.

DF1.11 — AC2(b) asserts the engine unit orders after `systemd-tmpfiles-setup.service`. That is expressible only because DF2.10 ships a *system* unit; had it been a user unit, cross-manager `After=` would not work and the ordering would have had to rest on the user manager's own start. DF2.10's choice was made to keep DF1.11's AC valid as written.

DF1.10 — Infra Prereq :114 declares an in-image pi catalog addressed by `QDS_PI_CATALOG_DIR` and calls an unlocatable catalog 'a hard blocker', to be 'probed in DF2.10's image'. DF2.10 owns the pinned pi and therefore that surface; its AC2 measurement of the pinned version's registry-file shape is the thing that de-risks the blocker, but DF2.10 makes no catalog-directory claim. If DF1.10 needs the catalog path pinned in the image, that obligation must land in DF2.10 before it is built.

Sprint wrap-up (R10 §2a) — the drafted sprint-status.yaml line for DF2.10 says 'thread --image/--setup-script/--registry-auth through create()'. The story deliberately threads only two flags and justifies it (systemd is the boot hook, so `--setup-script` and its 10 KiB cap are irrelevant). The yaml note should be corrected to two flags or it overstates the shipped scope.
